newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds sustain gains, outperform Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds sustain gains, outperform Brazil.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much higher Friday as an initial spurt thanks to market friendly U.S. economic indicators was sustained by reported spread trades out of Brazil to Argentina.

Traders said that after a week which started off on a poor note, this session showed investors may be returning to Argentina, as the market sustained its early surge even though U.S bonds turned lower on profit-taking after an initial jump.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 6/8 to 83, while the local dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.55 to 119.10.
An analyst at a large foreign bank said Argentina outperformed much of the rest of Latin American markets this session, largely because investors sold Brazilian bonds and bought Argentine ones.
Argentine bonds have lagged the rest of Latin American markets for much of the year and many traders and analysts have predicted that Argentina would start catching up as growth bounces back.
Still, the main impulse for Argentina's market this session was the culmination of a week with U.S. indicators showing growth is moderating.
The U.S. October employment data released Friday showed non-farm payrolls rose by 210,000 in October, against market expectations of a rise of 212,000.
"The outcome of the U.S. employment report and the lead in the polls by President Bill Clinton are positive as they mean the U.S. long bond yield is likely to remain stable," said a trader.
Traders predicted the coming week would be less volatile. "I think the market will be more stable in coming days," the analyst said.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 6.95 percent from 6.55 percent.
